rationale: In the landmark discovery cohort establishing LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621415), Willim et al. (2024) specifically documented varying types of seizures in exactly 6 of 33 affected individuals (18.2%). Subsequent literature (such as Khan et al., 2026) describes additional probands presenting with seizures (e.g., tonic seizures in a patient carrying de novo p.Pro887Leu), raising cumulative reported human cases to 7 of 34 (~20.6%). Both the original cohort figure (18.2%) and the aggregate data establish that seizure penetrance in LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder remains approximately ~18-21%, which is significantly lower than high-penetrance postsynaptic density synaptopathies/channelopathies such as SYNGAP1 encephalopathy (>80%).

evidence.text: Willim et al. identified 33 individuals with dominant neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous LRRC7 variants and noted that varying types of seizures occurred in exactly six patients.

source.title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors

evidence.text: Khan et al. identified a novel de novo missense variant in LRRC7 in an additional proband presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and tonic seizures, further supporting seizure susceptibility while expanding the clinical denominator.

source.title: Further Evidence for LRRC7 Gene Involvement in Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Novel Variant
source.quote: Here, we investigated a proband presenting global developmental delay (GDD), tonic seizures, failure to thrive, mild microcephaly, intellectual disability (ID), and hypotonia.

evidence.text: Hall et al. confirm that haploinsufficient mouse models of LRRC7 manifest seizures alongside learning and memory deficits, corroborating the biological link between LRRC7 disruption and seizure phenotypes.

conflicts: While 6/33 (18.2%) is the exact rate in the primary discovery cohort of Willim et al. (2024), inclusion of subsequently reported individual probands (e.g., Khan et al. 2026) shifts the cumulative literature frequency slightly to 7/34 (20.6%).

new_directions.question_text: What specific electroclinical seizure semiologies and EEG abnormalities characterize LRRC7-related epilepsy compared to SYNGAP1 or STXBP1 encephalopathies?
new_directions.rationale: Willim et al. noted 'varying types of seizures' in the 6 patients, but specific semiology (e.g., absence, tonic, myoclonic, or focal) and EEG signatures are not systematically mapped across variant classes.

new_directions.question_text: Does seizure penetrance correlate with specific domain locations in LRRC7, such as the LRR domain versus the PDZ domain?
new_directions.rationale: Functional assays in Willim et al. revealed differential effects of LRR domain vs PDZ domain variants on PP1 binding and synaptic targeting, which may drive phenotypic heterogeneity in epileptogenesis.
